evidence.text: It reports oracle-bone 小 meaning ‘small,’ citing 《粹》1004 小雨; it separately reports 小食 as an afternoon time expression and 小采 as an evening expression. evidence.field: 少 entry, graphic and usage account
evidence.text: It says oracle-bone forms of 小/少 could have four dots and were used in the same way; later the three-dot graph was used for 小 and four-dot form for 少. In bronze forms, the lowest dot of 少 extended into a diagonal stroke. The page cites bronze uses of 少 for ‘few’ and ‘young,’ and a later case where 少 is read as 小. This supports graphic differentiation and shared early use, but does not settle the more specific proposed sand-grain referent.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—小

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Character Database
evidence.text: The database states that 少 and 小 were originally one graph depicting fine sand grains, with ‘small’ as the original meaning; in bronze inscriptions the bottom dot of 少 became a diagonal stroke, distinguishing it from 小. This is a clear assertion of the shared-origin analysis, while CUHK presents that relationship alongside competing accounts of 小’s earliest formation.
evidence.title: 漢字「少」：字形演變

evidence.source: 《常用漢字二百字探源》 (PDF), entry 小
evidence.field: 字形探源 and 字義探源, pp. 20–21
evidence.text: The book lists oracle-bone and bronze examples and says both scripts write 小 with three dots. It reports disagreement over what the dots depict, including raindrops, scattered objects, or fine smallness; it judges an abstract indicator-of-smallness analysis plausible. It says later dots lengthened into lines and rejects Shuowen’s parsing of the seal form as 八 plus 丨 as an error based on the later shape. It cites oracle-bone examples 小雨, 小風, and 小牢 for the ‘small’ use. This provides another account of the dots and the alleged graphic reinterpretation, not independent proof that they depict sand.
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The dictionary reproduces Xu Shen’s analysis: 小 means ‘the subtle/small among things’ and is analyzed as 八 and 丨, ‘seen and divided.’ It preserves this as a historical dictionary account. Its modern senses include small in size or quantity, make smaller, briefly, young, low-ranking, and humble self-reference, with classical citations; the page does not establish a chronological order among those senses.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》：小

evidence.field: 小 headword; PDF p. 76, printed p. 64; scanned headword and continuation checked on PDF p. 77, printed p. 65
evidence.text: The scanned entry identifies 小 as pictographic and interprets its marks as tiny grains of dust or sand, calling it an early graph of 沙; it says the graph was extended to mean ‘small,’ opposite 大, and gives that sense in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions. It cites 《粹》1004 for 小雨, then describes extensions to low status, contempt, and youth. It says the current form was corrupted in bronze inscriptions and treats Shuowen’s 八-plus-丨 account as an explanation of that altered form. The adjacent 少 entry says 小 and 少 were originally one graph, with similar use in oracle-bone texts, and later differentiated; its explanation continues onto printed p. 65. Direct scan inspection confirms the cited headword and passage. Forms checked against pixels: 小, 少, 沙, 八, 丨, 大, and the text’s citation 《粹》1004. The scan supports what this author asserts; it does not settle the disputed sand-grain interpretation.

gaps: The small-sand-grain depiction / 小 as an early graph of 沙 analysis is disputed; sources also analyze the dots as abstract marks for smallness, and the depicted referent is not independently established.

The graph’s oracle-bone use meaning ‘small’ is reported with specific inscription citation 《粹》1004, but this research did not inspect a facsimile or establish an absolute date for that artifact. CUHK also reports separate time terms 小食 and 小采 without dates or a demonstrated semantic bridge from ‘small.’

No evidence here establishes that 沙 was borrowed phonetically using a word name for the depicted grains. Treating 小 as the source graph of 沙 remains an attributed proposal, not a proven sound loan; the sand-object name and pronunciation are unrecoverable from the consulted evidence.

The 小–少 graphic relationship is supported by sources describing an original shared graph and later differentiation, while the specific sand-grain analysis remains contested. Wiktionary reports an exceptional Middle Chinese s-/ɕ- alternation in a proposed word-family relationship, but the primary sources accessed here do not resolve the lexical relationship or independently document Schuessler’s argument.
No absolute dates were recovered for the cited bronze examples or their semantic extensions. Do not use modern dictionary gloss ordering as a chronology.

The character-specific official Unicode Unihan page https://www.unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=5C0F repeatedly failed to open. Current kMandarin xiǎo was checked in the supplied local source row; no separately inspectable official per-character URL could be verified.

For 雀, CUHK asserts 小 is a phonetic component, but a same-system reconstruction comparison for both 雀 and 小 was not completed. The local Baxter–Sagart file does not substitute for inspection of both exact rows, and the sound role should remain source-attributed rather than demonstrated here.
The local glyph candidates were not opened or visually inspected in this research; no claims are made from those files.

Whether the earliest dots depict grains of sand or are abstract marks for smallness remains disputed. No inspected evidence establishes the specific depicted object or a phonetic borrowing of 沙; the sand analysis is attributed to Ma Xulun, not demonstrated as a sound loan.

CUHK reports an oracle-bone usage 小雨 with the citation 《粹》1004, but this research did not inspect a facsimile or establish the artifact's absolute date. It reports time expressions and later bronze uses without dates or a demonstrated semantic bridge from ‘small.’
The 小–少 shared-graph and differentiation account is reported by CUHK, but the lexical and graphic details are not settled by the material inspected here.

CUHK reports 小 as a sound component in 雀. Local Baxter–Sagart rows are included for both graphs, but do not by themselves explain that source-attributed phonetic role; the individual character pages and a phonetic-history account were not independently verified.
The official Unicode individual-record endpoint for 小 returned an internal fetch error. Local reading rows are identified as local provenance, not externally confirmed records.

No Xiaoxuetang single-character form page or image was obtained in the inspected pages. The selected image is therefore the Commons modern seal-script redraw, not an ancient artifact image. The separate Sinica Character Database page states All Rights Reserved, so no image from that site is proposed.

字源’s claim that 小’s marks depict sand grains and that 小 was an early graph of 沙 is this author’s analysis; consulted references also support an abstract smallness-sign account. The original depicted referent remains unsettled. No inspected source establishes a phonetic borrowing of 沙 based on the name or pronunciation of depicted sand grains.

The 字源 entry reports oracle-bone 小雨 and other early meanings, but the underlying inscriptions were not inspected here; no absolute artifact dates or demonstrated semantic bridge for the time and status uses were established.
字源 PDF page 76 is printed p. 64; its continuation is PDF page 77, printed p. 65. Both scan images were directly inspected. No specific OCR correction was identified in the cited 小 passage.

The local reading row for 小 is current kMandarin metadata, not evidence about ancient sound relationships. The official individual Unicode Unihan record endpoint was not accessed in this research invocation.

The CUHK page attributes a sound role to 小 in 雀, but this invocation did not independently establish a historical sound relationship using inspected component and host readings in the same reconstruction system. Keep that role source-attributed and unresolved.
